## OPERATOR DECISION: delete (not tombstone)

The operator was presented with the two remediation options for the 13 orphaned reverse
bindings enumerated in the previous comment (`reverse_missing_forward`, REB-410…REB-422,
all pointing at deleted `ZZ-*TEST` fixture tickets from a retired isolated-test
environment) and chose, verbatim: **"delete."**

So the repair is: **remove the 13 orphaned `reverse[<jira_key>]` entries outright**, rather
than migrating them into `bindings-retired.json` as tombstones. Rationale consistent with
the diagnosis already on this ticket — every referenced local ticket is `deleted` test
scaffolding created under a different `env_id` (`ade0f2ef-…`, not the current
`01a1a015-…`), so there is no live pairing to preserve and nothing to un-retire later. A
tombstone would encode a Jira↔local relationship that was never real in this environment.

### Before-state (re-measured immediately prior to repair, read-only)

    unknown_event_types: 0
    binding_drift: would_terminal=0, local_gone=0, retired_overlap=0, dangling=0,
                   unbound_jira=0, absent_in_window_unprobed=950, indeterminate=5
    store_integrity: 13

All 13 are kind `reverse_missing_forward`, keys REB-410 through REB-422 contiguous —
identical to the enumeration recorded previously, so the fault is stable and the repair
target is exact. Only `store_integrity` alerts; every alerting `binding_drift` cell is
already 0.

Repair will be executed through a supported rebar door (no ad-hoc raw git in the tracker);
after/before fsck evidence to follow in a subsequent comment.
